head: VOSKI: offline translator app for iPhone for two people, one phone
dek: VOSKI is a new 99-cent offline translator app for two people talking on one iPhone or iPad: each person speaks in turn and the app reads the translation aloud. It was #64 in paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 24 November.
details: You pick two languages and tap the mic; the app works out who is speaking. Speech recognition, translation and voices run on the phone, without an AI chatbot or a server, after the language files download once. Which languages work depends on what your phone can translate on its own. It's a one-time purchase with no subscription, made by Dean Turpin, and needs iOS 26 or iPadOS 26; the listing says it collects no data.
where: iPhone and iPad (iOS 26 or later), $0.99 one-time
means: If you travel where data is expensive or patchy, this lets you have a back-and-forth conversation with someone without an internet connection.
todo: Pick your two languages while you still have Wi-Fi, so the language files are on your phone before the trip.
